entries.text: Invoice number. Every line of one order shares it. Invoice numbers starting with C are cancellations.
Product code. Some codes are not products: POST is postage, D is a discount, M is a manual adjustment, BANK CHARGES and AMAZONFEE are fees.
Product name. Missing on some lines.
Units of the product on the line. Negative for cancellations, returns and stock adjustments.
Date and time the invoice was created, from 2010-12-01 to 2011-12-09. The timezone is not stated.
Price of one unit in pounds sterling (GBP). Some lines have a price of zero.
Customer identifier. It is an ID, not an amount: group or count by it, never sum or average it. About a quarter of lines have no customer.
Country the customer lives in. Most lines are from the United Kingdom, so other countries rest on few lines.
Sales value of a line in GBP, Quantity times UnitPrice. Sales, turnover, income and money made all mean the sum of Revenue.
Each row is one product line on an invoice, not a whole order. Counting rows counts lines, not orders or customers.
Can mean the most units sold (sum of Quantity by Description) or the most money (sum of Revenue by Description). Ask which one when the question does not say.
Questions about customers only cover lines with a CustomerID. Lines without one are left out of any per-customer result.
Cancelled lines have a negative Quantity and negative Revenue, which lowers totals. Filter Quantity greater than 0 to look at sales only.
Many customers are wholesalers, so a single order can be very large and averages per line are skewed.
